findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted
findings.body: In `isAccessTokenId`, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut MATCHES the expected value, which is backwards — it should return false when it does NOT match. As written, the matcher will fail for the correct grant shortcut and pass for any other shortcut, making this test helper assert the wrong thing (effectively testing that the grant shortcut is NOT the expected one).

findings.title: Overwriting GRANT_TYPE on refresh may be incorrect for offline tokens
findings.body: In validateToken, `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN)` is unconditionally set when refreshing a token. This loses the original grant type context (e.g., device flow, CIBA) that produced the original token, and conflicts with session restored by `clientSessionCtx` built from stored client session, potentially producing inconsistent/incorrect token id encoding for subsequent refreshes of offline/CIBA/device sessions, which the PR explicitly aims to make visible for optimization.

findings.title: Potential race in lazy-refresh of grant maps
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily refresh grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps using ConcurrentHashMap, but updates are not atomic across both maps (two separate put calls), so concurrent threads could observe a `grantsByShortcuts` entry without the corresponding `grantsToShortcuts` entry (or vice versa), risking inconsistent round-trip encode/decode under concurrent load right after a new grant type provider is deployed.

findings.title: Wrong variable null-checked in constructor
findings.body: The constructor checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means a null `rawTokenId` will not be caught here and will later throw a NullPointerException elsewhere (or silently produce a malformed token id), with a misleading error message if the check were ever triggered.

findings.title: Backward-compat token ids without ':' prefix accepted silently
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId treats any token id without a ':' delimiter as an old/unencoded token id and returns UNKNOWN context without validation. This is a reasonable compatibility fallback, but there's no test or doc describing what happens for malformed ids that happen to contain a ':' but aren't actually encoded by this scheme (e.g., from a different IdP-issued string reused as a token id), which could throw unexpected IllegalArgumentException during introspection/userinfo instead of gracefully falling back as 'unknown'.
